Refactor the Sign-In Page to OTP (Initial Screen)

I need to refactor the Sign-In page from a Magic Link button to a Two-Step OTP (Code-Based) authentication flow.

Target File: src/app/auth/signin/page.tsx
Task: Replace the entire content of src/app/auth/signin/page.tsx with this code. This creates a state machine for the login process:
The Code:
code
Tsx
'use client'

import { signIn, useSession } from 'next-auth/react'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'

export default function SignIn() {
  const router = useRouter()
  const { data: session } = useSession()

  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [code, setCode] = useState('')
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
  const [step, setStep] = useState<'email' | 'code'>('email')
  const [error, setError] = useState('')

  const handleSendCode = async (e: React.FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setLoading(true)
    setError('')

    // NOTE: NextAuth does NOT support OTP directly on the email provider.
    // We will use the 'credentials' provider for a custom code-based login (like your esthetician app).
    // We will treat the 'code' screen as the main login mechanism.
    // For now, we simulate the code being '123456' for the next step.

    // In a production environment, this would be a real API call to send a code via Twilio/SES
    if (email.trim() === '') {
        setError('Please enter a valid email address.')
        setLoading(false)
        return
    }

    // MOCK: Simulate success and advance to code entry
    setTimeout(() => {
        console.log(`[MOCK] Sent verification code to ${email}. Code: 123456`)
        setStep('code')
        setLoading(false)
        setError('')
    }, 1000)
  }

  const handleLogin = async (e: React.FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setLoading(true)
    setError('')

    // NOTE: This is the actual login call using the *Credentials* provider for custom logic
    const result = await signIn('credentials', { 
        email, 
        code, // The user-entered code
        redirect: false,
    }) 

    setLoading(false)
    if (result?.error) {
      setError('Invalid code or credentials. Please try again.')
      console.error("Sign-in error:", result.error)
    } else if (result?.url) {
      // Success: Redirect to dashboard
      router.push('/dashboard')
    }
  }

  // UI Structure
  const renderContent = () => (
    <div className="w-full max-w-md p-8 rounded-2xl border border-[var(--border-strong)] bg-[var(--card-bg)] shadow-[var(--shadow-hover)] backdrop-blur-md">
      
      <div className="text-center mb-8">
        <div className="w-12 h-12 rounded-full flex items-center justify-center mx-auto mb-4 border-2 border-[var(--coral)] bg-white shadow-lg dark:bg-[#211e2f] dark:shadow-xl">
          <svg width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="var(--coral)" strokeWidth="2.5" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
            <path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14L21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path>
          </svg>
        </div>
        <h1 className="text-3xl font-bold text-[var(--text-primary)] font-big-shoulders mb-2">Creative Portal</h1>
        <p className="text-[var(--text-secondary)] text-sm">{step === 'email' ? 'Enter your email to receive a verification code.' : 'Enter the 6-digit code sent to your email.'}</p>
        {error && <p className="text-sm text-[var(--coral)] mt-3 font-semibold">{error}</p>}
      </div>

      {/* Step 1: Email Entry */}
      {step === 'email' && (
        <form onSubmit={handleSendCode} className="space-y-4">
          <Input 
            type="email" 
            placeholder="name@company.com" 
            value={email}
            onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
            required
            className="h-12 bg-[var(--bg-alt)] border-[var(--border-subtle)] text-[var(--text-primary)] focus:border-[var(--coral)] rounded-lg"
            disabled={loading}
          />
          <Button 
            type="submit" 
            disabled={loading}
            className="w-full h-12 bg-[var(--coral)] hover:bg-[#e55a5a] text-white font-bold uppercase tracking-wider rounded-lg transition-all hover:shadow-lg border-0"
          >
            {loading ? 'SENDING CODE...' : 'GENERATE VERIFICATION CODE'}
          </Button>
        </form>
      )}

      {/* Step 2: Code Entry */}
      {step === 'code' && (
        <form onSubmit={handleLogin} className="space-y-4">
          <Input 
            type="text" 
            placeholder="Enter 6-digit code" 
            value={code}
            onChange={(e) => setCode(e.target.value)}
            required
            maxLength={6}
            className="w-full h-12 text-center text-xl bg-[var(--bg-alt)] border-[var(--border-subtle)] text-[var(--text-primary)] focus:border-[var(--coral)] rounded-lg tracking-widest"
            disabled={loading}
          />
          <Button 
            type="submit" 
            disabled={loading}
            className="w-full h-12 bg-[var(--coral)] hover:bg-[#e55a5a] text-white font-bold uppercase tracking-wider rounded-lg transition-all hover:shadow-lg border-0"
          >
            {loading ? 'VERIFYING...' : 'SIGN IN WITH CODE'}
          </Button>
          <Button 
            type="button" 
            variant="ghost" 
            onClick={() => setStep('email')}
            className="w-full text-[var(--teal)] hover:bg-transparent"
          >
            Change Email
          </Button>
        </form>
      )}

      <div className="mt-6 text-center">
        <p className="text-xs text-[var(--text-muted)]">
          Secured by Luis Gilberto Ecosystem
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  )

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center px-4">
      {session && session.user ? router.push('/dashboard') : renderContent()}
    </div>
  )
}
```"
2. Update NextAuth API (The Core Logic)
The app now expects a credentials provider to handle the login. We need to create a new file that pretends to check the database for the code.
Prompt 2: Create Custom Credentials Provider
"I need to update the NextAuth API to handle the custom 2-step OTP sign-in process.
Target File: src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts
Task 1: Add Credentials Provider
We must add the CredentialsProvider to handle the email + code submission.
Action: Find the providers: [...] array and add this CredentialsProvider to it. Keep the existing EmailProvider as it is needed for the database session management.
The Code to Insert into providers: [...]:
code
Tsx
CredentialsProvider({
      name: "Credentials",
      credentials: {
        email: { label: "Email", type: "email" },
        code: { label: "Code", type: "text" }
      },
      async authorize(credentials) {
        if (!credentials?.email || !credentials?.code) {
          return null;
        }
        
        // --- AUTHENTICATION LOGIC ---
        // 1. Check database for a matching, valid, non-expired token.
        // 2. Since this is a MOCK, we just check for a hardcoded code.
        const HARDCODED_CODE = "123456";
        
        if (credentials.code === HARDCODED_CODE) {
          // MOCK SUCCESS: If code is correct, find the user by email
          const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email: credentials.email } });
          if (user) {
            // Success: Return user object to create session
            return { ...user, role: user.role, id: user.id };
          } else {
            // User does not exist, create a new one (Simulated sign-up)
            const newUser = await prisma.user.create({
              data: {
                email: credentials.email,
                name: credentials.email.split('@')[0],
                role: 'CLIENT',
              }
            });
            return { ...newUser, role: newUser.role, id: newUser.id };
          }
        }
        
        // Failure
        return null;
      }
    }),

Task 3: Final Verification
Restart the development server. The new flow will now appear, and you can log in using the mock code 123456."
